corrections.caveats: Evidence is three plots in /images with no table, CPU model, rustc version, flags or FreeType version; the numbers in claimed_speedup are read off the charts (approximate; checked against the images). The plots were last updated on 2020-09-05 (commits 'Freetype bench' and 'More data and be more color blind friendly'), when fontdue was far older than today's 0.9.4, and they have not been regenerated since. Benchmark code is public (dev/benches/rasterize.rs and layout.rs, criterion 0.3; the FreeType case only builds with the freetype_benchmark feature, freetype-rs 0.26). The comparison is not apples-to-apples: (1) fontdue::Font::from_bytes, run outside the timed loop, parses and flattens every glyph outline up front, with FontSettings.scale set to the exact benchmarked size, so the timed fontdue loop only rasterizes cached geometry; (2) the FreeType loop calls set_char_size and then load_char with LoadFlag::RENDER for every character, so it parses each glyph (glyf or CFF charstrings), applies FreeType's default hinting and renders, while fontdue does not hint. The large CFF gap at small sizes (about 11x at 10 px/em) is consistent with charstring parsing and hinting landing only on the FreeType side. The layout benchmark compares with glyph_brush_layout 0.2.0 (a Rust library), not a C/C++ incumbent. fontdue began as a fork of font-rs and was rewritten; font-rs is a separate entry.

The orchestrator's hinting concern is confirmed in code, and the bigger asymmetry is that fontdue's glyph parsing and outline flattening happen at font load, outside the timed loop.

corrections.baseline: harfbuzzjs ^0.4.13 (HarfBuzz compiled to WebAssembly, called from JavaScript), not native HarfBuzz; opentype.js also compared; the rasterization rows compare with FreeType through the freetype2 (node-freetype2) Node native binding
corrections.hardware: Apple M1 Pro MacBook Pro, 16 GB (meta block of docs/.vitepress/data/benchmarks.json, generated 2025-12-16, 1 run); the README table states no hardware
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Bun 1.3.4 runtime running the TypeScript sources via bun test ./bench/ (from benchmarks.json meta and package.json); no build flags apply
corrections.claimed_speedup: README table vs harfbuzzjs: path extraction 16x, text to SVG 1.2-1.5x, Latin 1.5x, Arabic 1.2x, Hebrew 1.6x, Hindi 3.6x, Myanmar 10.5x, CJK 1.3-1.5x; vs opentype.js 4x to 86x; the README says it 'outperforms harfbuzzjs (WebAssembly) and opentype.js across all benchmarks'. The committed results file (docs/.vitepress/data/benchmarks.json, ops/s, M1 Pro, Bun 1.3.4) gives different ratios vs harfbuzzjs (derived from page data): English paragraph 1.48x, Russian/Ukrainian/Belarusian 1.18-1.26x, Greek 1.17x, Chinese/Japanese/Korean 1.26-1.31x, Hebrew 1.24x, Arabic 1.04x, Thai 1.58x, Khmer 2.25x, Hindi 3.25x, Myanmar 10.60x, glyph path extraction 50x, text to SVG 5.3-7.1x; with no features on mixed text text-shaper is slower (82,320 vs 90,800 ops/s, 0.91x). Only the Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and CJK rows (about 1.2-1.5x) do comparable work on both sides. The same file reports rasterization vs FreeType (freetype2 binding) of 1.50x at 12 px to 10.21x at 200 px (derived from page data), with the caveats below.
corrections.workload: OpenType shaping of word to paragraph texts in Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Thai, Khmer, Myanmar and CJK (Noto fonts and texts from the reference/rustybuzz submodule; Cyrillic, Greek and CJK use macOS's Arial Unicode.ttf), plus glyph path extraction, text to SVG and grayscale/LCD rasterization, timed under Bun with a batch timer (bench/utils.ts measure: shaping uses 10 warmup calls, then 3 timed batches of 100 calls).
corrections.caveats: Baseline is harfbuzzjs, the WebAssembly build of HarfBuzz driven from JavaScript, not native HarfBuzz; each timed harfbuzzjs call creates a buffer, copies the text into WASM memory, guesses segment properties, shapes and destroys the buffer, while text-shaper reuses its buffers (shapeInto). Several headline rows time different work: (1) Path extraction: getGlyphPath caches paths per font and glyph in a WeakMap (src/render/path.ts), so after warmup the text-shaper side times a cache lookup while harfbuzzjs glyphToPath rebuilds an SVG path string on every call. (2) Complex scripts: bench/shaping.test.ts calls shapeInto without script or direction, and UnicodeBuffer.addStr never sets them (script defaults to 'Zyyy', direction LTR), so the cached shape plan enables only the default features (ccmp, locl, rlig, rclt, calt, liga, kern, mark, mkmk; src/shaper/shape-plan.ts) and no RTL reversal runs. Arabic joining forms and Indic/Myanmar/Khmer script features from the fonts are therefore not applied on the text-shaper side, while harfbuzzjs guesses script and direction and runs the full script shaper; the Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Khmer, Thai and Myanmar ratios compare unequal work, and the output is not checked against HarfBuzz. (3) Rasterization vs FreeType: rasterizeGlyph defaults to hinting off and reuses the cached glyph path (hinted runs reuse a hinted-glyph cache), while FreeType's loadGlyph({render: true}) loads, hints with default flags and renders every call through a Node native binding. The README table does not match the committed results file (e.g. path extraction 16x vs 50x; text to SVG 1.2-1.5x vs 5.3-7.1x; Arabic 1.2x vs 1.04x), so its source run is unknown; 'outperforms across all benchmarks' is contradicted by the no-features row (0.91x). The results file is a single run from 2025-12-16, while the bench code read here is the 2026-07 HEAD. Bench fonts and texts come from the reference/rustybuzz git submodule (harfbuzz/rustybuzz @ 51d99b8), so they are public; the Cyrillic, Greek and CJK cases need macOS's /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf.
